# Wald

> Wald distribution.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```javascript
var wald = require( '@stdlib/stats/base/dists/wald' );
```

#### wald

[Wald][wald-distribution] (inverse Gaussian) distribution.

```javascript
var dist = wald;
// returns {...}
```

The namespace contains the following distribution functions:

<!-- <toc pattern="*+(cdf|pdf|mgf|quantile)*"> -->

<div class="namespace-toc">

-   <span class="signature">[`cdf( x, mu, lambda )`][@stdlib/stats/base/dists/wald/cdf]</span><span class="delimiter">: </span><span class="description">Wald distribution cumulative distribution function.</span>
-   <span class="signature">[`logcdf( x, mu, lambda )`][@stdlib/stats/base/dists/wald/logcdf]</span><span class="delimiter">: </span><span class="description">Wald distribution natural logarithm of cumulative distribution function.</span>
-   <span class="signature">[`logpdf( x, mu, lambda )`][@stdlib/stats/base/dists/wald/logpdf]</span><span class="delimiter">: </span><span class="description">Wald distribution natural logarithm of probability density function (PDF).</span>
-   <span class="signature">[`mgf( t, mu, lambda )`][@stdlib/stats/base/dists/wald/mgf]</span><span class="delimiter">: </span><span class="description">Wald distribution moment-generating function (MGF).</span>
-   <span class="signature">[`pdf( x, mu, lambda )`][@stdlib/stats/base/dists/wald/pdf]</span><span class="delimiter">: </span><span class="description">Wald distribution probability density function (PDF).</span>
-   <span class="signature">[`quantile( p, mu, lambda )`][@stdlib/stats/base/dists/wald/quantile]</span><span class="delimiter">: </span><span class="description">Wald distribution quantile function.</span>

</div>

<!-- </toc> -->

-   <span class="signature">[`mean( mu, lambda )`][@stdlib/stats/base/dists/wald/mean]</span><span class="delimiter">: </span><span class="description">Wald distribution expected value.</span>
-   <span class="signature">[`mode( mu, lambda )`][@stdlib/stats/base/dists/wald/mode]</span><span class="delimiter">: </span><span class="description">Wald distribution mode.</span>
-   <span class="signature">[`skewness( mu, lambda )`][@stdlib/stats/base/dists/wald/skewness]</span><span class="delimiter">: </span><span class="description">Wald distribution skewness.</span>
-   <span class="signature">[`stdev( mu, lambda )`][@stdlib/stats/base/dists/wald/stdev]</span><span class="delimiter">: </span><span class="description">Wald distribution standard deviation.</span>
-   <span class="signature">[`variance( mu, lambda )`][@stdlib/stats/base/dists/wald/variance]</span><span class="delimiter">: </span><span class="description">Wald distribution variance.</span>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

<!-- eslint no-undef: "error" -->

```javascript
var wald = require( '@stdlib/stats/base/dists/wald' );

/*
* The Wald (inverse Gaussian) distribution is parameterized by mean `mu` and shape parameter `lambda`.
*/

var mu = 20.0;
var lambda = 60.0;

// Compute the mean:
var m = wald.mean( mu, lambda );
// returns 20.0

// Compute the mode:
var md = wald.mode( mu, lambda );
// returns ~12.361

// Compute the variance:
var s2 = wald.variance( mu, lambda );
// returns ~133.333

// Compute the standard deviation:
var sigma = wald.stdev( mu, lambda );
// returns ~11.547

// Compute the skewness:
var skew = wald.skewness( mu, lambda );
// returns ~1.732

// Compute the excess kurtosis:
var kappa = wald.kurtosis( mu, lambda );
// returns 5.0

// Evaluate the PDF at x = 20.0:
var y = wald.pdf( 20.0, mu, lambda );
// returns ~0.0345

// Evaluate the CDF at x = 20.0:
var p = wald.cdf( 20.0, mu, lambda );
// returns ~0.607

// Evaluate the logPDF at x = 20.0:
var ly = wald.logpdf( 20.0, mu, lambda );
// returns ~-3.365

// Evaluate the logCDF at x = 20.0:
var lp = wald.logcdf( 20.0, mu, lambda );
// returns ~-0.499

// Compute the 50th percentile:
var q = wald.quantile( 0.5, mu, lambda );
// returns ~17.193

// Evaluate the MGF at t = 0.01:
var m0 = wald.mgf( 0.01, mu, lambda );
// returns ~1.23
```

</section>
